2027-03-26.title: Passion Friday (Good Friday)
2027-03-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The Passion of Christ (Part II): the pierced side and the burial
2027-03-26.alt: Passion Friday (Dukha Velli). A day of fasting and abstinence. There is no celebration of the Holy Qurbana today; the Church keeps the service of the Passion, the veneration of the Cross, the procession and the burial of the Cross. The order and the hours follow your diocese and parish.
2027-03-26.verse: When Jesus had received the wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
theo: The Church begins this day of sorrow with a father and a son climbing a mountain. God says to Abraham, “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I shall show you.” Every word tightens the knot: your son, your only son, whom you love. Abraham lays the wood on Isaac's shoulders and carries the fire and the knife himself, “So the two of them walked on together.” Then the boy asks the question that echoes through the whole Bible: “The fire and the wood are here, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?” Abraham answers, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” On Moriah the hand of Abraham is stopped and a ram caught in a thicket dies in Isaac's place. On Calvary no hand is stopped. The Father does not spare his own Son, and the Son carries the wood of his own sacrifice up the hill. The question of Isaac is answered at last by John the Baptist: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” What Abraham was asked to give and was spared, God gives and does not spare. That is why the Church reads Genesis 22 today: to show that the Cross is not a human tragedy that God turned to good, but the gift of the Father who so loved the world that he gave his only Son.

Isaiah's fourth song of the Servant is read on this day by Christians everywhere, because it reads like an eyewitness account written centuries before. “He was despised and rejected by others; a man of suffering and acquainted with infirmity.” The prophet's community confesses its mistake: they thought he was punished by God for his own sins. Then the truth breaks in: “But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have all turned to our own way, and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.” And the Servant goes silent to his death: “like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.” Paul draws out what this means for us. Christ did not die for the good and the deserving: “For while we were still weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.” “But God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.” The Cross is the proof. Whoever doubts that God loves him should look at the crucifix and read what is written there: you were worth this to me. And Paul goes further: through one man's disobedience sin and death entered; through the one man Jesus Christ the free gift of grace overflows to the many.

The Passion is read today in two parts, woven from the Gospels of Luke, Matthew and John. Jesus is mocked, blindfolded and struck; he is led to the council, to Pilate, to Herod, and back to Pilate. Three times Pilate finds no case against him. Pilate's wife sends a message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man, for today I have suffered a great deal because of a dream about him.” Pilate washes his hands, and the crowd cries, “His blood be on us and on our children!” The Church reads these words with great care. The Second Vatican Council teaches that what happened in the Passion “cannot be charged against all the Jews, without distinction, then alive, nor against the Jews of today” (Nostra Aetate 4), and the Catechism reminds us that sinners, all of us, were the authors of Christ's sufferings (CCC 597–598). Indeed the blood of Christ is on us: not as a curse but as the blood that cleanses, sprinkled on all who are saved. Then come the words from the Cross. To his executioners: “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.” To the thief who asks to be remembered: “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.” To his Mother and the beloved disciple: “Woman, here is your son… Here is your mother.” Then, “I am thirsty”, and they lift a sponge of sour wine to his lips. “It is finished.” Darkness covers the land, the curtain of the temple is torn, the earth shakes, and a Roman officer says, “Truly this man was God's Son!” In the second part a soldier pierces his side, “and at once blood and water came out”, and Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus lay him in a new tomb in a garden. The Fathers saw in that blood and water the Holy Qurbana and Baptism, and the Church herself born from the side of the new Adam asleep on the Cross.

How a family can follow the rites of Passion Friday, step by step (the order and names differ a little between dioceses, so follow your parish). First, the fast: on this day the faithful keep fast and abstinence, and many keep silence, switch off the television and take only kanji. Second, the service of the Passion in church, usually in the morning or afternoon: the prayers of the day, the readings from Genesis, Isaiah and Romans, and the long reading of the Passion (Part I), followed by the Passion sermon. There is no Holy Qurbana on this day: the altar stands bare, for the one Sacrifice is contemplated on the Cross itself. Third, the veneration of the Cross (Sliva Vandanam): the crucifix is shown to the people, and one by one they come forward, kneel and kiss the wounds of the Lord. Fourth, the procession with the Cross through the streets or around the church, praying the Way of the Cross; many walk to hills of pilgrimage such as Malayattoor with wooden crosses on their shoulders. Fifth, the second part of the Passion (John 19:31–42) and the burial: the body of the Lord, the crucifix or an image, is laid in a tomb prepared with flowers, and the people pass by in prayer. Sixth, the bitter drink (kaippuneer): at the end each one takes a sip of a bitter drink, recalling the sour wine offered to the thirsty Lord on the Cross, and promising to share his bitterness rather than run from it. At home, many families read or sing the Puthen Pana of Arnos Pathiri, especially the lament of the Mother, and keep the evening in quiet. Nothing in these rites is theatre. Each step is a way of standing with Mary and John at the foot of the Cross, where the world was redeemed.
conn: Isaac carries the wood up Moriah (Genesis 22:6); Jesus goes out “carrying the cross by himself” (John 19:17). The ram dies in Isaac's place; the Lamb of God dies in ours (John 1:29).
Not one bone of the Passover lamb was to be broken (Exodus 12:46); John sees this fulfilled when the soldiers do not break the legs of Jesus (John 19:36).
“For my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink” (Psalm 69:21); on the Cross Jesus says “I am thirsty” and receives the sour wine (John 19:28–30). The kaippuneer of Passion Friday keeps this memory.
“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” (Psalm 22:1; Matthew 27:46) is the first line of a psalm that ends in praise and the conversion of the nations (Psalm 22:27).
The curtain that hid the Holy of Holies is torn (Matthew 27:51); through his flesh Christ has opened for us a new and living way into the sanctuary (Hebrews 10:19–20).
As Eve was formed from the side of the sleeping Adam (Genesis 2:21–22), the Church is born from the opened side of Christ: blood and water, the Eucharist and Baptism (John 19:34).
altar: Today there is no Holy Qurbana, and the bare altar teaches as loudly as any sermon. The sacrifice we offer every Sunday is not another sacrifice but this one: the one offering of Calvary made present on the altar under the signs of bread and wine.

When we kiss the Cross today, we kiss the same Lord we receive in Holy Communion. The Body that hung on the tree is the Body that is given to us; the Blood that flowed from his side is the Blood in the chalice.
outline: Silence before the Cross. Ask: what did my salvation cost?
Point 1 · God will provide the lamb
Moriah and Calvary: the Father who does not spare his Son.
Point 2 · By his bruises we are healed
The Servant who bore our sins in silence.
Point 3 · The words from the Cross
Forgiveness, Paradise, a Mother, thirst, completion.
The Church born from his side; kneeling with Mary.
A family in a dark church, waiting in line to kiss the feet of the crucified Lord, and a child lifted up to kiss them too.
live: Fast and abstain today, and offer the hunger for someone who suffers.
Name one person who has hurt you and pray today: Father, forgive them.
Take part in the service of the Passion and the veneration of the Cross with your whole family.
Read the Passion (John 19) or the Puthen Pana at home, and leave the television and phone aside.
fathers: Death trampled our Lord underfoot, but he in turn treated death as a highroad for his own feet. He submitted to death of his own will, so that he might overthrow death against death's will. He went out to Golgotha carrying his Cross, and from the Cross he called the dead out of Sheol.

He who hung the earth in its place is hanged; he who fixed the heavens is fixed to a tree; the Master is insulted, God is murdered. He is the Lamb that was slain and taken from the flock, and he has rescued us from slavery to freedom, from darkness to light, from death to life.
magis: Jesus' violent death was not the result of chance; it belongs to the mystery of God's plan, which also uses human sin for our salvation.
The Passion cannot be charged against all Jews of that time or of today; all sinners were the authors of Christ's sufferings.
The death of Christ is both the Paschal sacrifice and the sacrifice of the New Covenant; it is unique and completes all other sacrifices.
It is love to the end that gives Christ's sacrifice its value of redemption and reparation.
Mary's union with her Son in the work of salvation is shown at the foot of the Cross.
The Church was born from the pierced side of Christ asleep on the Cross.
saints: Saturday 27 March: Great Saturday. Sunday 28 March: the Resurrection of our Lord (Uyirppu). Monday 29 to Saturday 3 April: the first week of Resurrection, the week of the newly baptised.
2027-03-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Lamb of God, you carried the wood of your sacrifice up the hill, and you were wounded for our transgressions. We adore you and we bless you, for by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Forgive us as you forgave those who crucified you; remember us in your kingdom as you remembered the thief; give us your Mother as you gave her to the beloved disciple. Let the blood and water from your side wash us and feed us, and let us not run from your Cross but stand beside it with Mary, until we see your glory. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: Abraham was spared his only son; the Father did not spare his.
“By his bruises we are healed”: the Servant bore our sins in silence.
From the Cross: forgiveness, Paradise, a Mother, and “It is finished.”
2027-03-26.action: Forgive one person today, by name, as Jesus forgave from the Cross.
2027-03-26.question: What does the Cross ask of me today, and from whom am I still running?
catechism: God's saving plan in the Passion.
Who is responsible for Christ's death.
kidsaint: One of the men crucified beside Jesus said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” Jesus promised him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.” (Later tradition calls him Dismas.) Lesson: it is never too late to say sorry to Jesus!
2027-03-26.special: Passion Friday (Good Friday): fasting and abstinence; no Holy Qurbana; service of the Passion, veneration of the Cross, procession, burial of the Cross and kaippuneer.
term: The bitter drink given to the faithful at the end of the Passion Friday service in the Syro-Malabar Church. It recalls the sour wine offered to Jesus when he said “I am thirsty” (John 19:28–29), and the bitterness of the Passion that the disciple promises to share.

family.explain: Jesus died on the cross because he loves us. Even on the cross he forgave the people who hurt him, and he promised heaven to the thief who said sorry. He gave his own Mother Mary to be our mother. Today the church has no Qurbana; we kiss the cross and say thank you.
family.intention: We pray for all who are suffering, and we thank Jesus for his love.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to forgive today, like Jesus did?”

illus: In a house near Pala, a grandfather kept an old wooden crucifix that had belonged to his own father. Every Passion Friday after the church service he placed it on the table, lit a small lamp, and the whole family, from the youngest grandchild to the oldest aunt, came one by one to kiss the feet of the Lord. One year his teenage grandson, home from college in Delhi, hung back. “It is just wood, appacha,” he said. The old man did not argue. He turned the crucifix over and showed him, carved small on the back in his father's hand, the date of the year their family had lost everything in a flood, and the words ‘He did not leave us.’ The boy was silent for a long time. Then he came and knelt.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified for us, we kneel before your Cross. Let us keep watch with you in silence. Amen.
share: Take your son, your only son… whom you love (Genesis 22:2). What did my salvation cost the Father?
He was wounded for our transgressions (Isaiah 53:5). Which of my sins do I see in his wounds?
Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34). Whom do I find it hardest to forgive?
Here is your mother (John 19:27). Have I taken Mary into my home?
It is finished (John 19:30). What must I finally hand over to him today?
pm.resp: Lord, by your holy Cross, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may be faithful at the foot of the Cross.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in love of his name and in faithfulness to his covenant.
For all who suffer: the sick, the persecuted, the lonely, the dying.
For those who have lost faith, that the Cross may speak to them of love.
For our families, that we may forgive one another as Christ forgave.
pm.close: Father, you did not spare your own Son but gave him up for us all. Look on your family gathered at the Cross, and through his blood forgive us, heal us and make us one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today there is no Qurbana. The altar is bare and the tabernacle is empty. The Church stands in silence at the foot of the Cross, where the one Sacrifice was offered once for all.

We began with Abraham and Isaac on the mountain. The boy asked, “Where is the lamb for a burnt offering?” and his father answered, “God himself will provide the lamb.” On Moriah the knife was stopped. On Calvary it was not. The Father gave his only Son, whom he loves, and the Son carried the wood of his own sacrifice.

Isaiah saw him centuries before: “He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities… and by his bruises we are healed.” He did not open his mouth. And Paul tells us why: “God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.” Not for the good, but for sinners. For you and for me.

Listen to his words from the Cross. “Father, forgive them.” He forgives those who are killing him. “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” He opens heaven to a thief. “Here is your mother.” He gives us Mary. “I am thirsty.” He thirsts for our love. “It is finished.” Not ‘I am finished’, but ‘the work is complete’.

Who killed him? The Church answers honestly: not a people, not a nation, but sin, our sin. That is why today we do not point at anyone. We beat our own breasts, and then we come to kiss the wounds that heal us.

When you take the bitter drink today, remember the thirst of the Lord. Do not run from the bitterness of your own cross. Stand with Mary, forgive someone by name, and keep this evening in silence. We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus died on the cross. He did it because he loves us so much and wanted to take away all our sins.
On the cross Jesus said sorry for the people who hurt him: ‘Father, forgive them.’ Can you forgive someone today?
When we kiss the cross today, let us say: ‘Thank you, Jesus, for loving me so much!’

opts.a: Where do I stand at the Cross?
intro: The Passion is full of people. Some washed their hands, some mocked, some carried the Cross, some wept, one confessed. Today we ask: where do I stand?

points.h: Pilate and Herod: avoiding the truth
points.apply: Ask where you wash your hands of what is right.

points.h: Simon and the women: carrying and weeping
sub: Simon compelled to carry the cross.
Jesus cares for them even now.
points.apply: Carry someone's burden this week without complaint.

sub: A pagan soldier sees how he dies.
The first confession at the Cross.
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross today slowly, confessing Jesus as Son of God.

concl: Every one of us has a place in the Passion.
Let us leave Pilate's basin and come with Simon, the women and the centurion.
opts.resolve: Today I will choose my place at the Cross: to carry, to weep for my sins and to confess Jesus as Son of God.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the story of the Passion is crowded with people. Today, as we stand before the Cross, let us look at some of them, because each of us is somewhere in that crowd.

Herod was glad to see Jesus because he hoped to see some sign. When Jesus gave no answer, he and his soldiers mocked him. Pilate knew Jesus was innocent, yet he took water, washed his hands before the crowd, and handed him over (Matthew 27:24). Luke tells us that Herod and Pilate became friends that same day (Luke 23:12). The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD and his anointed (Psalm 2:2). Where do I wash my hands of what is right, to keep my comfort?

Then there is Simon of Cyrene, a man coming in from the country, made to carry the Cross behind Jesus (Luke 23:26). He did not choose it, but he carried it. And there were women beating their breasts and wailing. Jesus, on his way to death, turned to them: do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children (Luke 23:28). Even then he was caring for others. Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? (Lamentations 1:12).

And at the end, a pagan officer watched him die. When the earth shook, the centurion and those with him said: truly this man was God's Son! (Matthew 27:54). Isaiah had said that kings would shut their mouths because of him, for they would see what they had not been told. The first full confession at the Cross came from a foreigner.

Today there is no Qurbana; the Church kneels in silence. Let us leave Pilate's basin. Let us carry someone's cross with Simon, weep for our sins with the women, and kneel with the centurion to say: truly, this is the Son of God, who died for me. Amen.

opts.a: Love for enemies, a tomb in a garden
intro: Paul says Christ died for us while we were still weak, still sinners, still enemies. The day ends in a garden, where two hidden disciples find courage.

sub: Rarely will anyone die for a righteous person.
God's heart that will not give us up.
points.apply: Pray today, by name, for someone you consider an enemy.

sub: The gift of grace through one man, Jesus Christ.
The promise in the first garden.
points.apply: Bring your heaviest sin to the Cross today and trust his mercy.

sub: Joseph of Arimathea, a secret disciple.
points.apply: Show your faith openly this week in one place where you have kept it hidden.

concl: Christ died for his enemies and turned sin into an occasion of grace.
At his tomb, the timid become brave.
opts.resolve: Today I will pray for an enemy by name and resolve to stop hiding my faith.
homily: Dear friends, Paul says something astonishing in today's Epistle: rarely will anyone die for a righteous person, though perhaps for a good person someone might actually dare to die. But God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us (Romans 5:7–8). Not for friends only, but for those who were his enemies.

Through Hosea, God says of his unfaithful people: how can I give you up? My heart recoils within me (Hosea 11:8). The Cross is the place where God's heart refuses to give us up. If Christ died for his enemies, then I cannot hate mine. Let us pray today by name for someone we find hard to forgive.

Paul also compares Adam and Christ. If many died through the one man's trespass, much more has the grace of God abounded for the many through the one man, Jesus Christ (Romans 5:15). In the first garden, after the first sin, God already promised that the offspring of the woman would strike the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). Today that promise is fulfilled on the wood of the Cross.

And at evening, there was a garden near Calvary with a new tomb. Joseph of Arimathea, a disciple of Jesus, though a secret one, asked Pilate for the body. Nicodemus, who had first come by night, brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes (John 19:38–39). Isaiah had said that his grave would be with the rich. Those two men had hidden their faith. At the Cross they found courage.

Today, as we kiss the wounds of the Crucified, let us pray for our enemies, bring our heaviest sin to his mercy, and decide not to hide our faith any longer. The tomb in the garden is not the end. It is the seed of Easter. Amen.

intro: Theme: “When Jesus had received the wine, he said, ‘It is finished.’ Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.”
The lamb that God provides, the Servant wounded for us, the words from the Cross, and the Church born from the pierced side.

points.h: God himself will provide the lamb
sub: Your son, your only son, whom you love.
On Calvary no hand is stopped.
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
points.apply: Look at a crucifix for five minutes today and say only: you were given for me.

points.h: By his bruises we are healed
sub: The sins of all laid on one.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
But God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.
points.apply: Bring one hidden sin to the Cross today, and plan to confess it in Easter week.

sub: No one is to blame but sin.
q: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have all turned to our own way, and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.”
points.apply: Forgive one person by name today, and if possible tell them.

sub: The Church born from the new Adam.
q: They gave me poison for food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Take the kaippuneer today as a promise not to run from your own cross.

concl: What Abraham was spared, God gave; what we deserved, Christ bore; what was torn open on the Cross is the door of the Church.
Kneel, kiss the wounds, forgive, and stand with Mary until the morning comes.
2027-03-26.resolve: Today keep the fast with love, venerate the Cross with your family, forgive one person by name, and keep the evening in silence.
